lessons_from_past_refresh_mistakes: Never guess a sibling/child URL by pattern-matching a filename. Always fetch the parent page first with a prompt like 'list every markdown link verbatim as [text](url), do not summarize or omit any' - generic 'extract full detailed content' prompts silently drop links roughly half the time, which is how 9 real pages got missed on the very first crawl of this skill.

Do the verbatim-link audit on EVERY page in sources.json when refreshing, not just the ones involved in a 404 - the two are independent failure modes (a 404 means a guessed URL is wrong; missing links on a 200-OK page is a separate, quieter failure that leaves no error to notice).

docs.n8n.io serves a real, consistent app-level 404 page (title 'Page Not Found', a 'Suggested Pages' list, no Cloudflare challenge) - if you hit that, don't assume rate-limiting; it means the exact path is wrong. Go back to the nearest real parent page and re-derive links from there.

When checking whether a topic (e.g. OAuth2) is truly undocumented vs. just unfetched, ask a precise 'quote verbatim any section about X' or 'list every link' question rather than a generic summarization question - the generic version once produced a misleading half-answer ('mentioned in the overview but not detailed here') for content that flatly doesn't exist on that page.

Runtime/engine-behavior claims (does X trigger automatic retry? can declarative style do Y at execution time? does throttling require hand-written code?) cannot be verified from the /connect/create-nodes/ authoring-docs tree alone, even exhaustively crawled - that tree covers how to author a node, never what the engine does with it afterward. Two false runtime claims were made in a single planning session this way: (1) 'declarative can't throttle between requests, so a rate-limited API forces programmatic style' - actually backwards, declarative gets a free engine-level batching throttle (see 22-reference-batching.md) that programmatic doesn't; (2) 'transforming data before/after a request forces programmatic style' - actually false, declarative's preSend/postReceive hooks handle single-request transformation including full body-format changes like JSON-to-XML (see 21-reference-routing-hooks.md); (3) 'throwing failure.cause: rate-limited triggers n8n's automatic retry' - false, that field is unread by the action-node retry path, only consumed by polling-trigger backoff (see 23-reference-node-runtime-settings.md). All three were caught only because a user directly challenged the claim rather than accepting it. When a plan asserts a *runtime* behavior, verify against a docs.n8n.io page outside /connect/create-nodes/ (e.g. the workflow-builder-facing 'work-with-nodes' or 'handle-rate-limits' pages) or against n8n-io/n8n source directly (routing-node.ts, workflow-execute.ts, interfaces.ts are the load-bearing files so far) - never present authoring-docs-derived inference as confirmed runtime fact.

A page can be captured with all its links intact but its CONTENT silently truncated to a one-line summary - ux-guidelines.md's AI-tool Output section was stored as one sentence when the live page had a full section (modes, rationale, ID-always-included default, contrasting Simplify section). Pass A (links) cannot detect this. In Pass B, compare each fetched section's length against the stored file; a stored file much shorter than its live source is a red flag, and for sections that specify behavior (defaults, required fields), ask for that section verbatim.

When an n8n CLI or engine command appears not to support something, check the input before blaming the tool: read the loader or command source first. Unrecognized node type for a custom node meant a wrong type prefix in a hand-written fixture (CUSTOM.<name> vs <package>.<name>), not a missing capability.

Don't infer "retry never happened" from n8n execution runData: each node's runData array has one entry per node run, not per Retry On Fail attempt. Check executionTime or N8N_LOG_LEVEL=debug per-attempt log lines before concluding a runtime feature failed.
Make every new check or script prove it can fail before trusting a PASS: run it once against a known-bad input (the .old project, a mutated expected count, a deliberately broken anchor).
